chapter: Violin, clarinet and the family name
title: Violin at five and the Junior Philharmonic
summary: Starting a half-size violin at five, learning chords, serious legitimate training, concert master in school and in the Los Angeles Junior Philharmonic.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: That's great. You started playing -- your first instrument was violin?
I was actually about five years old when I had my -- when I really got into actually playing and studying hard on the violin, when I was about five. My father bought me

a half-size violin because I was much too small to play even a three-quarter size violin, so I had a little half-size one. And I played it and I learned how to play chords on it and -- which also taught me to automatically become a banjo player, because I learnt the fingerings of the chords and it was just a matter of picking up the banjo and finding out the different distance between the notes as in comparison with my half-size violin. So, I was an automatic, built-in banjo player.
You say you were five years old before you did any serious studying.
What did you do before five?

Well, I tinkered around with whatever was around the house. I used to get the mandolins and play with them, the round-backed, beautiful, inlaid mandolins and I would tinker around and just try to play anything that I could put my hands on. But then, my dad gave me this violin and then I had to study everyday, from the time I was five years old.
What kind of music were you playing? What were you studying?

I studied legitimate music. Just a legitimate background. By the time I got to junior high school, I was the concert master in the band. I was always the concert master in every orchestra that I ever played. I played with the Junior Philharmonic Orchestra here as a child in Los Angeles. I

think the conductor there was Rothstein, Rosenthal, Rothstein or something. I can't think of that man's name. He was the conductor of the Los Angeles Philharmonic Orchestra. So I played there with the Junior Philharmonic Orchestra when I was in junior high school and in high school, legitimate music.
